simple.meaning: אָנָּא (ʼânnâʼ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “oh now!.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 50:17. The surrounding context includes family, covenant, commandment.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָנָּא (H577) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אָנָּא (ʼânnâʼ) / H577 is traced through Genesis 50:17, Exodus 32:31, 2 Kings 20:3, Nehemiah 1:5 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: ‘You shall tell Joseph, “Now please forgive the disobedience of your brothers, and their sin, because they did evil to you.” ’ Now, please forgive the disobedience of the servants of the God of your father.” Joseph wept when they spoke to him.

timeline.evidenceText: ‘You shall tell Joseph, “Now please forgive the disobedience of your brothers, and their sin, because they did evil to you.” ’ Now, please forgive the disobedience of the servants of the God of your father.” Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
Moses returned to Yahweh, and said, “Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made themselves gods of gold.
“Remember now, Yahweh, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.

and said, “I beg you, Yahweh,† “Yahweh” is God’s proper Name, sometimes rendered “LORD” (all caps) in other translations. the God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness with those who love him and keep his commandments:

Lord,‡ The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.” I beg you, let your ear be attentive now to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayer of your servants, who delight to fear your name; and please prosper your servant today, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man.”
Then I called on Yahweh’s name:
Yahweh, truly I am your servant.
Save us now, we beg you, Yahweh!
Save us now, we beg you, Yahweh!
and said, “Remember now, Yahweh, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in your sight.” Then Hezekiah wept bitterly.
I prayed to Yahweh my God, and made confession, and said,
Therefore they cried to Yahweh, and said, “We beg you, Yahweh, we beg you, don’t let us die for this man’s life, and don’t lay on us innocent blood; for you, Yahweh, have done as it pleased you.”

He prayed to Yahweh, and said, “Please, Yahweh, wasn’t this what I said when I was still in my own country? Therefore I hurried to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that you are a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and you relent of doing harm.

definitions.full: H577. annah or anna אָֽנָּ֫א interjection (from אָהּ and נָא , q. v.) a strong particle of entreaty, ah, now! I (or We) beseech thee! often followed by an imperative; Gen 50:17 (to Joseph) וג נָא שָׂא ׳אָנָּא Ah, now ! forgive, we pray, etc., Exod 32:31 (to God); elsewhere always followed by ׳י or אֲדֹנָי Psa 118:25 (twice in verse); Neh 1:5 , 11 ; Dan 9:4 . Written אָֽנָּ֫ה 2Kin 20:3 (= Isa 38:3 ) Jonah 1:14 ; 4:2 ; Psa 116:4 ; 116:16 . אנב (perhaps spring, leap , so Dl HA 65, Pr 114 , inferred from Assyrian annabu , hare ; against this Nö ZMG 1886, 734 ).
definitions.rootNote: or אָנָּה ; apparent contracted from 160 and 4994 ;
